q: The groups of atoms that are attached to the carbon backbone of organic compounds are known as ____ groups.
e: The groups of atoms that are attached to the carbon backbone of organic compounds are known as functional groups. The functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the organic family.

q: The most important common techniques are infrared (IR), ultraviolet/visible (UV/Vis), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and ____ spectrometry.
e: The most important common techniques are infrared (IR), ultraviolet/visible (UV/Vis), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and mass spectrometry. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: A chemical test is typically a fast reaction performed in a test tube that gives a visual clue (a colour change, precipitate, or ____ formation).
e: A chemical test is typically a fast reaction performed in a test tube that gives a visual clue (a colour change, precipitate, or gas formation). Gas is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Alkenes mixed with 1% $KMnO_4$ solution result in ____.
e: Alkenes mixed with 1% KMnO4 solution result in decolourisation. Decolourisation is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Alkynes passed through ammoniacal $Cu_2Cl_2$ solution give a ____ coloured precipitate.
e: Alkynes passed through ammoniacal Cu2Cl2 solution give a red coloured precipitate. Red is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Alcohols warmed with acidified $K_2Cr_2O_7$ solution change from orange colour to ____ colour.
e: Alcohols warmed with acidified K2Cr2O7 solution change from orange colour to green colour. Green is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Aldehydes heated gently with Fehling's solution give a ____ coloured precipitate.
e: Aldehydes heated gently with Fehling's solution give a reddish-brown coloured precipitate. Reddish-brown is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ketones mixed with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNP) solution give a deep-____ coloured precipitate.
e: Ketones mixed with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNP) solution give a deep-orange coloured precipitate. Orange is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Carboxylic acids mixed with saturated $NaHCO_3$ solution result in the evolution of ____.
e: Carboxylic acids mixed with saturated NaHCO3 solution result in the evolution of CO2. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Primary amines reacted with $CHCl_3$ in the presence of alkali produce an unpleasant ____.
e: Primary amines reacted with CHCl3 in the presence of alkali produce an unpleasant smell. Smell is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The presence of a carbonyl group such as aldehyde or ketone can be easily tested by using a solution of ____.
e: The presence of a carbonyl group such as aldehyde or ketone can be easily tested by using a solution of 2,4-DNP. Aldehydes have a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: Fehling's solution is an alkaline solution containing copper(____) ions.
e: Fehling's solution is an alkaline solution containing copper(II) ions. II is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Infrared (IR) spectroscopy is the study of the absorption of light by a compound, in the ____ region of electromagnetic spectrum.
e: Infrared (IR) spectroscopy is the study of the absorption of light by a compound, in the infrared region of electromagnetic spectrum. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: The relationship between the energy (E) and the frequency ($\nu$) or wavelength ($\lambda$) of the electromagnetic radiation is described by ____'s equation.
e: The relationship between the energy (E) and the frequency () or wavelength () of the electromagnetic radiation is described by Planck's equation. Wavelength is the distance from one wave crest to the next.

q: Wavenumber (measured in $cm^{-1}$) which is the reciprocal of the ____, is one way to describe the frequency of electromagnetic radiation.
e: Wavenumber (measured in cm-1) which is the reciprocal of the wavelength, is one way to describe the frequency of electromagnetic radiation. Wavenumber counts how many waves fit into one centimetre.

q: Stretching is a vibration that occurs along the bond line and changes the bond ____.
e: Stretching is a vibration that occurs along the bond line and changes the bond length. Length is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Bending is a vibration that occurs between two bonds and changes the bond ____.
e: Bending is a vibration that occurs between two bonds and changes the bond angle. Angle is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Only those stretching and bending motions that change the ____ moment of a molecule give rise to the absorption of infrared radiation.
e: Only those stretching and bending motions that change the dipole moment of a molecule give rise to the absorption of infrared radiation. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: Light atoms, for example, vibrate at higher frequencies than heavier atoms and multiple bonds vibrate at higher frequencies than ____ bonds.
e: Light atoms, for example, vibrate at higher frequencies than heavier atoms and multiple bonds vibrate at higher frequencies than single bonds. Single is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The instrument used to obtain an infrared spectrum is called an IR ____.
e: The instrument used to obtain an infrared spectrum is called an IR spectrometer. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: The presence of hydrogen bonds in molecules also affects the ____ of the absorption bands.
e: The presence of hydrogen bonds in molecules also affects the shape of the absorption bands. A hydrogen bond is the strong intermolecular pull from H attached to N, O, or F toward another N, O, or F.

q: The OH bond of alcohols usually has an absorption in the range of 3200-3600 $cm^{-1}$, while the OH bond of carboxylic acids occurs in the range of ____ $cm^{-1}$.
e: The OH bond of alcohols usually has an absorption in the range of 3200-3600 cm-1, while the OH bond of carboxylic acids occurs in the range of 2500-3300 cm-1. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: An alkane lacks functional groups whereas an alkene and an alkyne have functional groups which are carbon-carbon double bond and carbon-carbon ____ bond, respectively.
e: An alkane lacks functional groups whereas an alkene and an alkyne have functional groups which are carbon-carbon double bond and carbon-carbon triple bond, respectively. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: The most common functional groups in organic compounds other than hydrocarbons are carbonyl (C=O), hydroxyl (OH), carboxyl (COOH), carboalkoxy (COOR), amine ($NH_2$) and carboxamide (____).
e: The most common functional groups in organic compounds other than hydrocarbons are carbonyl (C=O), hydroxyl (OH), carboxyl (COOH), carboalkoxy (COOR), amine (NH2) and carboxamide (CONH2). A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: The identification of the organic compound is based on simple chemical tests and ____ techniques that indicate the presence of specific functional groups.
e: The identification of the organic compound is based on simple chemical tests and spectroscopic techniques that indicate the presence of specific functional groups. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: Alkanes mixed with 1% $KMnO_4$ solution show no ____.
e: Alkanes mixed with 1% KMnO4 solution show no decolourisation. Decolourisation is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ethers boiled with HI and then reacted with $AgNO_3$ give a ____ coloured precipitate.
e: Ethers boiled with HI and then reacted with AgNO3 give a yellow coloured precipitate. Yellow is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Primary amides boiled with 20% NaOH solution result in the evolution of ____.
e: Primary amides boiled with 20% NaOH solution result in the evolution of NH3. NH3 is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Fehling's solution can be used to distinguish aldehyde and ketone functional groups because aldehydes can be further oxidised to form carboxylic acids, but ketones cannot be oxidised ____.
e: Fehling's solution can be used to distinguish aldehyde and ketone functional groups because aldehydes can be further oxidised to form carboxylic acids, but ketones cannot be oxidised easily. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: When the clear blue Fehling's solution is warmed with an aldehyde, the reddish-brown precipitate of ____ is formed.
e: When the clear blue Fehling's solution is warmed with an aldehyde, the reddish-brown precipitate of Cu2O is formed. Aldehydes have a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: Chemical tests are handy but not always practical for the identification of compounds with complex ____.
e: Chemical tests are handy but not always practical for the identification of compounds with complex structures. Structures is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The spectroscopic techniques can be performed quickly on small amounts of a compound and can provide much more information about the compound's ____.
e: The spectroscopic techniques can be performed quickly on small amounts of a compound and can provide much more information about the compound's structure. Structure is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Additionally, spectroscopic techniques are also non-____ techniques compared to methods using chemical reactions.
e: Additionally, spectroscopic techniques are also non-destructive techniques compared to methods using chemical reactions. Destructive is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Because electromagnetic radiation has wave-like properties, it is characterised by either its frequency or its ____.
e: Because electromagnetic radiation has wave-like properties, it is characterised by either its frequency or its wavelength. Wavelength is the distance from one wave crest to the next.

q: High frequencies, large wavenumbers, and short wavelengths are associated with high ____.
e: High frequencies, large wavenumbers, and short wavelengths are associated with high energies. Energies is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Photons in the infrared radiation region can cause bond ____ in molecules.
e: Photons in the infrared radiation region can cause bond vibrations in molecules. Infrared spectroscopy identifies groups by the frequencies of light they absorb as bonds vibrate.

q: The frequency of the absorbed radiation matches the frequency of the bond or group that ____.
e: The frequency of the absorbed radiation matches the frequency of the bond or group that vibrates. Frequency is how many wave crests pass a point each second.

q: Homonuclear diatomic molecules (e.g., $N_2$) which have no dipole moments are IR ____.
e: Homonuclear diatomic molecules (e.g., N2) which have no dipole moments are IR inactive. Dipole moment measures how polar a bond or molecule is.

q: On the other hand, heteronuclear diatomic molecules (e.g., CO) which have dipole moments are IR ____.
e: On the other hand, heteronuclear diatomic molecules (e.g., CO) which have dipole moments are IR active. Dipole moment measures how polar a bond or molecule is.

q: Each stretching and bending vibration occurs with a characteristic frequency which depends on the bond strength and the ____ of the atoms.
e: Each stretching and bending vibration occurs with a characteristic frequency which depends on the bond strength and the masses of the atoms. Frequency is how many wave crests pass a point each second.

q: It takes more energy to stretch a bond than to ____ it.
e: It takes more energy to stretch a bond than to bend it. Bend is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: When a sample is irradiated with electromagnetic radiation in the infrared region, an IR spectrum is obtained as a plot of the percent transmittance or absorbance of radiation versus the ____ of the radiation transmitted.
e: When a sample is irradiated with electromagnetic radiation in the infrared region, an IR spectrum is obtained as a plot of the percent transmittance or absorbance of radiation versus the wavenumber of the radiation transmitted. Wavenumber counts how many waves fit into one centimetre.

q: Different functional groups produce bond absorptions at different locations and ____ on the IR spectrum.
e: Different functional groups produce bond absorptions at different locations and intensities on the IR spectrum. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: The important factors that influence the intensity of an absorption band are polarity of the bond and number of ____.
e: The important factors that influence the intensity of an absorption band are polarity of the bond and number of bonds. Bonds is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The higher bond polarity and more number of bonds in molecules will give a more intense absorption ____.
e: The higher bond polarity and more number of bonds in molecules will give a more intense absorption band. Band is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The broad shape of the absorption band for O-H results from the hydrogen bonding of the OH groups between ____.
e: The broad shape of the absorption band for O-H results from the hydrogen bonding of the OH groups between molecules. A hydrogen bond is the strong intermolecular pull from H attached to N, O, or F toward another N, O, or F.

q: Consider N-H stretches in amine and amide which are medium intensity and width compared to O-H stretches; N-H stretch is narrow and weak while the O-H stretch is broad and ____.
e: Consider N-H stretches in amine and amide which are medium intensity and width compared to O-H stretches; N-H stretch is narrow and weak while the O-H stretch is broad and strong. Amines are organic bases with a nitrogen that can accept a proton.
